eyebrow: Enterprise Security Architecture, GRC & Risk Management · Chapter One
subtitle: Lesson 3 · Revisited at Enterprise Scale

code:
Earlier in this path, defense in depth meant:
  one system, layered controls around it.

At enterprise scale, the "thing" is:
  a federation of business units, subsidiaries,
  and acquired companies -- each with its own
  legacy tech, risk tolerance, and regulation.
caption: Layering now has to span the whole federation, not stack more tools on one app.

eyebrow: Six layers an enterprise has to coordinate

steps.label: Identity
steps.sub: one IdP, SSO, and conditional access every BU plugs into

steps.label: Network
steps.sub: segmentation between business units, subsidiaries, OT and IT

steps.label: Data, Endpoint, Detection
steps.sub: shared classification/DLP, fleet-wide EDR, a SOC that sees across BUs

steps.label: Governance
steps.sub: a shared minimum baseline plus a tracked exception process

code:
Attackers used a third-party HVAC vendor's
credentials to reach a vendor-management segment --
then moved into point-of-sale and cardholder data.

The controls existed.
The segmentation between business functions
didn't actually isolate them.
caption: A segmentation failure between business functions, not a single missing patch.

eyebrow: What actually works at this scale

steps.label: Centralized minimum baseline
steps.sub: every business unit must meet it, regardless of legacy tech

steps.label: Tracked exception / waiver
steps.sub: documented, time-bound, owned -- not a silent or permanent gap

subtitle: The same technical risk, two different correct postures.
